vectors.description: A well-formed proof with a valid Ed25519 signature and in-window timestamp
vectors.reason: Signature verifies against the signer key and ts is within skew

vectors.description: Proof whose JWS signature bytes were altered
vectors.reason: A mutated signature must fail EdDSA verification

vectors.description: Proof whose signed requestHash was altered after signing
vectors.reason: The reconstructed canonical payload no longer matches the signature

vectors.description: Valid proof verified against a different agent public key
vectors.reason: Signature does not verify under an unrelated key

vectors.description: Authentically signed proof whose timestamp is far outside the skew window
vectors.reason: ts is 10000s before now with a 300s skew — replay/stale guard must reject

vectors.description: Proof under profile org.kya-os/response-proof.envelope whose responseHash binds the full result envelope; verified against the received result with a mutated _meta
vectors.reason: Under prf=org.kya-os/response-proof.envelope the verifier hashes the received result with the top-level _meta removed, so a _meta-only mutation never invalidates the binding

vectors.description: Envelope-profile proof verified against a result whose structuredContent was swapped in flight (unauthenticated under the body-only profile)
vectors.reason: Envelope coverage authenticates structuredContent/isError/resultType — the recomputed responseHash must mismatch the bound one

vectors.description: Envelope-profile proof whose signature-covered prf claim was stripped after signing
vectors.reason: prf is a covered claim: without it the reconstructed payload no longer matches the signature — a downgrade to body-only semantics must be a hard fail

vectors.description: Proof carrying an unrecognized prf value
vectors.reason: Unknown response-proof profiles are rejected fail-closed — never verified under weaker (body-only) semantics

vectors.description: Proof whose requestHash is over the 1.x legacy shape {method: <tool name>, params: <arguments as received>}, verified against the tools/call request as sent
vectors.reason: During 1.x a verifier accepts a requestHash over the legacy shape with the arguments as received (SPEC.md §7.3)

vectors.description: Proof whose requestHash is over the 1.x legacy shape with every _kyaos* argument removed, verified against the tools/call request as sent
vectors.reason: During 1.x a verifier accepts a requestHash over the legacy shape with the control arguments removed (SPEC.md §7.3)

vectors.description: Proof whose requestHash is over the 1.x legacy shape of a call to another tool with the same arguments
vectors.reason: The hash is over none of the three shapes of the call held, so the request mismatches

vectors.description: Proof whose delegationChainDigest binds a three-credential chain (two credential objects and a VC-JWT leaf), verified against that chain
vectors.reason: The chain digest recomputed over the supplied credentials, root first, equals the signed delegationChainDigest (SPEC §7.8)

vectors.description: The same proof verified against another copy of the same chain: proof metadata outside the credential signature edited, and the three signatures written with padding, a line break, and spare bits set
vectors.reason: A credential is digested by what its issuer signed and the signature bytes, so a copy that differs in nothing signed has the same digest

vectors.description: Denial proof (no responseHash) whose delegationChainDigest binds the chain the server refused, verified against that chain as a refusal (expected.outcome: denied)
vectors.reason: A refusal binds no response and still binds what was presented, so a verifier that asks for a refusal can hold it against the refused chain

meta.reason: Delegation del-orchestrator-worker widens scopes beyond parent del-user-orchestrator: records:delete

vectors.description: The same denial proof verified against the chain it refused, by a verifier that supplies the chain and states no outcome
vectors.reason: A chain supplied without an outcome asks whether the server accepted it. The proof records a refusal, so a matching digest must not pass: it shows what was presented, not what was allowed

meta.reason: Delegation del-orchestrator-worker widens scopes beyond parent del-user-orchestrator: records:delete

vectors.description: Chain-binding proof verified against a chain whose middle credential was re-issued under the same id with a wider scope
vectors.reason: Every id and parent link matches, so delegationRef cannot tell the chains apart; the recomputed chain digest must mismatch the signed one

vectors.description: Chain-binding proof whose signature-covered delegationChainDigest was stripped after signing
vectors.reason: delegationChainDigest is a covered claim: without it the reconstructed payload no longer matches the signature

vectors.description: Authentic proof that names its credential by delegationRef and carries no delegationChainDigest, verified against a chain
vectors.reason: A verifier that is given a chain must not accept a proof that binds none: an equal delegationRef is not evidence of which chain was evaluated

vectors.description: Chain-binding proof verified against the bound chain with the VC-JWT leaf signature rewritten in the base64 alphabet (+ and / for - and _)
vectors.reason: A JWS segment is base64url. A compact JWS whose signature is not has no signed form, so the chain has no digest and no proof binds it, though a decoder of both alphabets reads the same bytes

vectors.description: Authentic proof whose delegationChainDigest binds the chain and whose delegationRef names the chain root, verified against that chain
vectors.reason: A proof that binds a chain names its last credential: delegationRef must be the reference derived from the presented (leaf) credential

vectors.description: Proof binding a single credential whose id is longer than 256 UTF-16 code units, with delegationRef the SHA-256 of the id
vectors.reason: An id too long to record is referred to by sha256 of its UTF-8 bytes, and a verifier derives the same reference from the credential

vectors.description: Chain-binding proof that names the bound chain, held against another delegation of the same sub-agent, which another party issued
vectors.reason: A proof names the delegation the call was made under by delegationRef and delegationChainDigest, so it is refused beside any other delegation of its subject: a party on the path that holds another cannot swap it in

vectors.description: Denial proof for a presented credential object whose signature fails under two ancestors that verify, held against that credential alone as a refusal
vectors.reason: A server examines the presented credential before any ancestor, so a refusal of one that does not verify binds the presented credential alone, not the chain it was presented under

vectors.description: Proof binding a single credential object whose arrays and objects nest 64 levels deep, as deep as a credential may nest
vectors.reason: A credential object nested 64 levels deep has a signed form, so its digest is taken and the proof binds it: an implementation must read that deep, whatever its bound or its stack

vectors.description: Authentic proof carrying the chain digest an implementation that counts no nesting takes of a credential object nested 65 levels deep, verified against that credential
vectors.reason: A credential object nested more than 64 levels deep has no signed form, so the chain has no digest and no proof binds it, however deep the implementation reading it could go

vectors.description: Proof binding a single VC-JWT whose payload nests 64 levels deep, with delegationRef the id that payload shows
vectors.reason: A VC-JWT payload nested 64 levels deep is read as JSON, so the credential shows its id and a proof that binds it names it

vectors.description: Denial proof binding a single VC-JWT whose payload nests 65 levels deep and naming no credential, verified against that VC-JWT as a refusal (expected.outcome: denied)
vectors.reason: A VC-JWT payload nested more than 64 levels deep is not read as JSON, so the credential shows no id and a proof that binds it carries no delegationRef. It still has a digest, taken over its segments as received

vectors.description: Denial proof binding a single VC-JWT whose payload holds an integer of 4301 digits, naming the credential by the id that payload shows, verified against that VC-JWT as a refusal (expected.outcome: denied)
vectors.reason: JSON sets no limit on the length of a number, so the payload is read whatever its numbers hold, and a number plays no part in the id: an implementation whose parser refuses a long number derives no id, and rejects a proof it must accept

meta.reason: JWT envelope signature is not valid: signature verification failed

vectors.description: Proof binding a single credential whose id is U+001F alone, the last C0 control character, with delegationRef the SHA-256 of the id
vectors.reason: An id that holds a control character, U+0000 to U+001F among them, is referred to by sha256 of its UTF-8 bytes: an implementation that stops the range short of U+001F names the credential by the id itself

vectors.description: Proof binding a single credential whose id is U+0020 alone, the first character past the C0 controls, with delegationRef the id itself
vectors.reason: U+0020 is no control character, so an id of it alone is referred to as it is: an implementation that runs the range past U+001F names the credential by a digest

vectors.description: Proof binding a single credential whose id is sha256: followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits and one more character, with delegationRef the id itself
vectors.reason: Only an id that reads as such a digest and nothing more is replaced by its own digest. One with a character after the 64 digits is kept: an implementation that matches the digest form at the start of the id alone names the credential by a digest

vectors.description: Proof binding a single credential whose id holds U+202E, a right-to-left override, with delegationRef the SHA-256 of the id
vectors.reason: An id that holds a format character, which prints as something other than it holds, is referred to by sha256 of its UTF-8 bytes: an implementation that hashes only ids with a control character names the credential by the id itself

vectors.description: Proof binding a single credential whose id holds U+200B, a zero-width space, with delegationRef the SHA-256 of the id
vectors.reason: An id that holds a format character, one that prints as nothing among them, is referred to by sha256 of its UTF-8 bytes: an implementation that hashes only ids with a control character names the credential by the id itself

vectors.description: Proof binding a single credential whose id holds U+034F, a combining grapheme joiner, with delegationRef the SHA-256 of the id
vectors.reason: An id that holds a code point that renders as nothing by default, whatever its general category, is referred to by sha256 of its UTF-8 bytes: an implementation that hashes only ids with a control or format character names the credential by the id itself

vectors.description: Proof binding a single credential whose id holds U+3164, a Hangul filler, with delegationRef the SHA-256 of the id
vectors.reason: An id that holds a code point that renders as nothing by default, whatever its general category, is referred to by sha256 of its UTF-8 bytes: an implementation that hashes only ids with a control or format character names the credential by the id itself

vectors.description: Proof binding a single credential whose id holds U+FE0F, a variation selector, with delegationRef the SHA-256 of the id
vectors.reason: An id that holds a code point that renders as nothing by default, whatever its general category, is referred to by sha256 of its UTF-8 bytes: an implementation that hashes only ids with a control or format character names the credential by the id itself

vectors.description: Proof binding a single credential whose id holds U+E0100, a variation selector outside the basic plane, with delegationRef the SHA-256 of the id
vectors.reason: An id that holds a code point that renders as nothing by default, whatever its general category, is referred to by sha256 of its UTF-8 bytes: an implementation that hashes only ids with a control or format character names the credential by the id itself

vectors.description: Proof binding a single credential whose id is the word unknown, with delegationRef the SHA-256 of the id
vectors.reason: An audit record names a credential that shows no id unknown, so an id written so is referred to by sha256 of its UTF-8 bytes and the word never stands for a credential: an implementation that keeps it names the credential by the id itself

vectors.description: Proof binding a single credential object whose issuer signed a member named __proto__, verified against that credential
vectors.reason: A member named __proto__ is a member like any other: it is part of the signed form, so of the digest. An implementation that drops it, or reads it as a prototype, computes another digest and rejects a proof it must accept

vectors.description: Denial proof binding a single VC-JWT whose payload holds the credential id twice, another id written ahead of the issuer's, naming the credential by the last of them, verified against that VC-JWT as a refusal (expected.outcome: denied)
vectors.reason: Of the members of one object that share a name the last is read, as JSON.parse reads them, so the credential shows the id written last: an implementation whose parser keeps the first, or refuses the payload, names another credential or none, and rejects a proof it must accept

meta.reason: JWT envelope signature is not valid: signature verification failed

vectors.description: Authentic proof carrying the chain digest an implementation that holds a number to RFC 8785 as it is written takes of a credential object holding 9007199254740993.5, verified against that credential
vectors.reason: A number is read as an IEEE 754 binary64 value before it is held to RFC 8785: 9007199254740993.5 reads as 9007199254740994, an integer of magnitude above 2^53 - 1, so the credential has no signed form and no proof binds the chain, though the number is no integer as written

vectors.description: The chain-binding proof with a character outside base64url (*) in its JWS signature segment
vectors.reason: A JWS segment is base64url: a segment with any other character is none, so the JWS does not verify

vectors.description: The chain-binding proof with four characters outside base64url (*!*!) in its JWS signature segment
vectors.reason: A decoder that passes over characters outside its alphabet reads the signature bytes from this segment, and must not: it is no JWS segment

vectors.description: The chain-binding proof with its JWS signature segment written in the base64 alphabet, padded (+ and / for - and _)
vectors.reason: A decoder of both alphabets reads the same bytes from this segment, but + and / are not base64url, so it is no JWS segment and the JWS does not verify

vectors.description: The chain-binding proof with a line break in its JWS signature segment
vectors.reason: A JWS segment holds no white space (RFC 7515 §2): a decoder that passes over it reads the signature bytes from this segment, and must not, so the JWS does not verify

vectors.description: The chain-binding proof with its JWS signature segment padded with = to complete its last group
vectors.reason: A JWS segment carries no padding (RFC 7515 §2): a decoder that reads padding reads the signature bytes from this segment, and must not, so the JWS does not verify

vectors.description: The chain-binding proof with a fourth segment appended to its JWS
vectors.reason: A compact JWS is three segments: a verifier that reads the first three of four verifies a JWS that is none

vectors.description: The chain-binding proof with a character outside ASCII (é) in its JWS header segment
vectors.reason: A JWS segment is base64url, and a character outside ASCII is not, so the JWS does not verify

vectors.description: The chain-binding proof with meta.requestHash altered after signing
vectors.reason: Every claim of meta is held to the payload the signature covers, rebuilt from it: the altered requestHash breaks the signature

vectors.description: The chain-binding proof with meta.nonce altered after signing
vectors.reason: The nonce is a claim the signature covers like the others: a verifier that compares only the delegation claims with the payload passes it

vectors.description: The chain-binding proof with meta.sessionId altered after signing
vectors.reason: The session is a claim the signature covers like the others: a verifier that compares only the delegation claims with the payload passes it

vectors.description: The chain-binding proof verified against the chain it binds and another call than the one it proves
vectors.reason: A proof binds the request it answers: held against another call, its requestHash mismatches, however well its chain matches

vectors.description: The chain-binding proof signed again with the server key, under a JWS header that names HS256
vectors.reason: A proof is an EdDSA JWS: a verifier refuses one whose header names another algorithm, though its signature verifies under the key

vectors.description: The chain-binding proof signed again with the server key, under a JWS header that names another key of its DID
vectors.reason: The header must name the key meta.kid names: a verifier refuses a proof whose header names another, though its signature verifies under the key

vectors.description: The chain-binding proof signed again with the server key, over a meta whose did is the delegating user's
vectors.reason: meta.kid names a key of the server DID, not of meta.did: a verifier refuses it, or one DID could sign proofs as any other

vectors.description: Chain-binding proof of a tools/call request that has no params, verified against that request
vectors.reason: A request is hashed as JCS({method, params}) with params left out where the request has none, so the proof binds the method alone
